org-object.statement: The organization's default authentication settings are one object, read and written at /authSettings. A separate GET /authSettings/lite returns the same model, but authFrequency, authCustomFrequency, lastSyncStartTime and lastSyncEndTime are not applicable to the Lite API.

quotes: Retrieves organization's default authentication settings information. (Lightweight version
Updates the organization's default authentication settings information.
`authFrequency`, `authCustomFrequency`, `lastSyncStartTime`, `lastSyncEndTime` are not applicable in the Lite API.
authSettingsLiteEndpoint = "/zia/api/v1/authSettings/lite"
cookie expiration duration after a user is first authenticated). This field is not applicable to the Lite API.

enum-values.statement: The spec lists these values: orgAuthType is ANY, NONE, SAFECHANNEL_DIR, MICROSOFT_ACTIVE_DIR, OPENLDAP_DIR, NOVELL_DIR, IBM_DOMINO_DIR, SUN_DIR or SMAUTH_ENTERPRISE_HOSTED; oneTimeAuth is OTP_DISABLED, OTP_TOKEN or OTP_LINK; passwordStrength is NONE, MEDIUM or STRONG; passwordExpiry is NEVER, ONE_MONTH, THREE_MONTHS or SIX_MONTHS. The Python SDK's passwordStrength and passwordExpiry docstrings give the same values.

quotes: Supported values: NONE, MEDIUM, STRONG.
Supported values: NEVER, ONE_MONTH, THREE_MONTHS, SIX_MONTHS.

ldap-and-saml-completeness.statement: Setting orgAuthType to an LDAP-based type requires a complete LdapProperties configuration, and enabling SAML (samlEnabled) requires complete SamlSettings.

quotes: User authentication type. Setting this to an LDAP-based authentication
Enabling SAML requires complete SamlSettings.

hosted-db-only.statement: passwordStrength and passwordExpiry apply to form-based authentication of hosted DB users only, not to SAML or directory authentication.

quotes: Password strength required for form-based authentication of hosted DB users. Not applicable for other authentication types (e.g. SAML SSO or Directory).
Password expiration required for form-based authentication of hosted DB users. Not applicable for other authentication types (e.g. SAML SSO or Directory).

one-time-auth.statement: oneTimeAuth only matters when orgAuthType is NONE; with SAML single sign-on enabled the one-time token is not applicable and the field has no effect.

quotes: When the orgAuthType is NONE, administrators must manually provide the password to new end users.
If SAML Single Sign-On is enabled, this one-time token is not applicable, and this field is ineffective.

kerberos-pwd-read-only.statement: kerberosPwd is read-only and can be set only through the generateKerberosPassword API. The Python SDK's update still serializes kerberosPwd into the request body.

quotes: kerberos_pwd (str): Read-only. Can only be set through the generate KerberosPassword API.
"kerberosPwd": self.kerberos_pwd,

scim-migration-flag.statement: directorySyncMigrateToScimEnabled disables directory synchronization for the user repository type so that SCIM provisioning or SAML auto-provisioning can be enabled; it is the setting for migrating from directory synchronization to SCIM.

quotes: Enable to disable directory synchronization for this user repository type so you can enable SCIM provisioning or SAML auto-provisioning.
Use this setting to migrate from directory synchronization to SCIM provisioning.

enum-vocabulary.summary: The legacy API reference page and the OpenAPI document give different value sets for the same authSettings fields.

quotes: Enum: [3 Items — NONE, LOW, HIGH]
Enum: [4 Items — NEVER, MONTHLY, QUARTERLY, SEMIANNUALLY]
Enum: [3 Items — OTP_DISABLED, OTP_ENABLED, OTP_MANDATORY]

positions.says: passwordStrength is NONE, LOW or HIGH; passwordExpiry is NEVER, MONTHLY, QUARTERLY or SEMIANNUALLY; oneTimeAuth is OTP_DISABLED, OTP_ENABLED or OTP_MANDATORY.
passwordStrength is NONE, MEDIUM or STRONG (and passwordExpiry and oneTimeAuth use the values in the enum-values claim).

enum-vocabulary.impact: A write built from the legacy page's value names (LOW, HIGH, MONTHLY, OTP_ENABLED) uses names the current spec and the Python SDK do not list; use the spec's values.

org-auth-type-vocabulary.summary: The legacy KB doc, the legacy API page and the OpenAPI document give different orgAuthType values.

quotes: Enum: [9 Items — ANY, NONE, LDAP_GROUP, LDAP_USER, SAML, AD_GROUP, AD_USER, ZIDENTITY, ZIDENTITY_GUEST]

positions.says: orgAuthType is ANY, NONE, LDAP_GROUP, LDAP_USER, SAML, AD_GROUP, AD_USER, ZIDENTITY or ZIDENTITY_GUEST. (The retired KB doc also listed KERBEROS_SERVICE and LDAP; neither source has them.)
orgAuthType is ANY, NONE, SAFECHANNEL_DIR, MICROSOFT_ACTIVE_DIR, OPENLDAP_DIR, NOVELL_DIR, IBM_DOMINO_DIR, SUN_DIR or SMAUTH_ENTERPRISE_HOSTED.

org-auth-type-vocabulary.impact: SAML, KERBEROS_SERVICE and LDAP are not valid orgAuthType values in the spec; SAML is turned on with samlEnabled, Kerberos with kerberosEnabled.

kerberos-pwd-write-behavior.title: What an update that includes kerberosPwd does
kerberos-pwd-write-behavior.detail: Unverified legacy statement: Setting kerberosPwd in an update_authentication_settings call is silently ignored; the field is accepted in the payload and appears to succeed but does not change the credential. No registered source states this. A lab update that sends kerberosPwd, then a read of the credential's effect, would settle it.
kerberos-pwd-write-behavior.blocks: whether rotating the Kerberos password through the settings update can succeed, fail or be ignored

auto-provision-scope.title: Who gets a user record when SAML auto-provisioning is on
auto-provision-scope.detail: Unverified legacy statement: With autoProvision true, any user whose IdP account is in scope for the ZIA SAML app has a ZIA user record created at first login, which can cause user-count surprises and license problems. No registered source states this. A vendor statement on auto-provisioning scope and licensing, or a lab login by an in-scope user, would settle it.
auto-provision-scope.blocks: answering how many users a tenant will end up with

scim-migration-reversibility.title: Whether turning off directory sync can be undone
scim-migration-reversibility.detail: Unverified legacy statement: Setting directory_sync_migrate_to_scim_enabled to true disables the legacy LDAP sync, and rolling it back is not self-service; confirm SCIM is fully operational first. No registered source states this. A vendor statement or a lab toggle back would settle it.
scim-migration-reversibility.blocks: advice on whether the migration flag is safe to try
